scores.claim_text: Microsoft was CoreWeave's largest customer, 62% of 2024 revenue ($1.2B recognized), under a Feb 2023 Microsoft MSA.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts CoreWeave in Microsoft (CIK 0000789019) filings; megacap_namecheck Microsoft subset
scores.M_value: Microsoft filings: 0 mentions of CoreWeave (10-K/10-Q/8-K, full history). megacap_namecheck Microsoft total_hits=0.
scores.interpretation: The buyer (Microsoft) never names CoreWeave in its SEC filings despite CoreWeave booking 62% of its revenue ($1.2B) from Microsoft. Per Heuristic 5, this asymmetry is benign-explainable: $1.2B of cloud spend is immaterial to Microsoft's ~$245B revenue, so non-disclosure by the buyer is expected and not a contradiction of CoreWeave's claim. However, the inverse concentration (one buyer = 62% of seller revenue) is itself the disclosed risk. No independent registry corroborates the Microsoft relationship directly; scored MODERATE (counterparty-side absence, but with benign explanation and strong internal/financial-statement consistency), not SEVERE.

scores.claim_text: March 2025 OpenAI MSA: OpenAI committed to pay up to ~$11.9 billion through October 2030.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts all-filer CoreWeave mentions (OpenAI is a private company, not an SEC filer); claim_evolution on CoreWeave CIK 0001769628
scores.M_value: OpenAI files no SEC reports (private), so no counterparty disclosure exists. EDGAR full-text shows CoreWeave named in 123 filings by other SEC filers (e.g. Core Scientific 8-Ks on HPC hosting), corroborating CoreWeave as a real recurring AI-infra counterparty, but none confirm the OpenAI dollar figure.
scores.interpretation: The $11.9B OpenAI commitment is (a) a FORWARD commitment signed days before cutoff (Mar 11 2025) contingent on delivery/availability, and (b) owed by a PRIVATE counterparty with no registry footprint. Per Heuristics 3 and 8, a private-counterparty forward commitment is not testable against any federal registry. The relationship's plausibility is supported by CoreWeave's broad ecosystem presence (123 EDGAR mentions) and the partly-offsetting $350M stock issuance to OpenAI disclosed in the same filing (an arm's-length structural detail consistent with a genuine deal). Honestly scored UNVERIFIABLE rather than manufacturing severity.

scores.claim_text: NVIDIA is a strategic investor in and key supplier to CoreWeave; CoreWeave deploys NVIDIA H100/H200/GH200 and GB200 NVL72 clusters.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts CoreWeave in NVIDIA (CIK 0001045810) filings; megacap_namecheck Nvidia subset
scores.M_value: NVIDIA names CoreWeave in 3 SEC filings (8-Ks dated 2024-08-28, 2024-11-20, 2025-02-26 — quarterly press releases). megacap_namecheck signal=RECURRING_RELATIONSHIP.
scores.interpretation: NVIDIA's own SEC filings independently corroborate the CoreWeave relationship across three consecutive quarters (RECURRING_RELATIONSHIP threshold met). This confirms CoreWeave as a named NVIDIA ecosystem partner/customer. Per Heuristic 4, NVIDIA's strategic-investor stake is not a material counterparty obligation, but the SUPPLIER/deployment relationship (NVIDIA naming CoreWeave in earnings materials) is corroborated. Scored PASS.

scores.claim_text: As of Dec 31 2024: 32 data centers, 250,000+ GPUs, 360+ MW active power, US in 15 states plus UK and Spain.
scores.M_value: EPA FRS registers 'COREWEAVE DATA CENTER / APPLICATION 2025-7064' at 2000 Galloping Hill Road, Kenilworth NJ (registry_id 110071993728). TRI/GHGRP: 0 (data centers are not >25kt CO2e industrial emitters). operational_scale_signal=FRS_PERMITTED_NO_INDUSTRIAL_REPORTING.
scores.interpretation: An EPA-registered CoreWeave data center exists, providing positive registry corroboration of real physical data-center operations. Per Heuristic 6 (name-variant fragility) and the prospectus's explicit tenant/leased-facility model, CoreWeave LEASES the bulk of its 32 data centers, which register under landlord/colocation-provider names rather than 'CoreWeave' — so EPA showing 1 of 32 under the tenant name is the expected result, not underdelivery. The scale claim is independently consistent with the audited balance sheet ($11.9B PP&E net, $3.2B construction-in-progress, $2.6B operating-lease ROU assets). Scored PASS: physical operations corroborated and the partial EPA hit-rate is fully explained by the tenant model (not a registry gap that should show more).

scores.claim_text: $15.1 billion of remaining performance obligations (RPO) as of Dec 31 2024, up 53% from $9.9B.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts CoreWeave in Microsoft filings (counterparty side of the largest committed contract)
scores.M_value: No federal registry records contracted backlog/RPO. Microsoft (largest RPO counterparty) discloses 0 mentions of CoreWeave. RPO is an audited ASC 606 disclosure within the same Deloitte/RSM-audited financial statements.
scores.interpretation: RPO is a backlog metric with no covering registry (Heuristic 8). The two largest counterparties are Microsoft (private-to-CoreWeave, immaterial to MSFT) and OpenAI (private, non-filer), so counterparty corroboration is structurally unavailable. The figure sits inside audited financials with deferred-revenue of $4.1B on the balance sheet ($768M current + $3.3B non-current), which is internally consistent with large upfront-paid committed contracts. No basis to assign underdelivery severity; honestly UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: Names AI customers Cohere, Mistral AI, OpenAI, Replicate, and enterprise customers Meta, IBM, Microsoft, Jane Street.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts CoreWeave in NVIDIA filings; megacap_namecheck (Microsoft, Meta, IBM subset)
scores.M_value: Megacap-side: Microsoft 0, Meta 0, NVIDIA 3 mentions of CoreWeave. Most named customers (Cohere, Mistral AI, OpenAI, Replicate, Jane Street) are private and file no SEC reports, so no counterparty disclosure is possible.
scores.interpretation: The named-customer list is a mix of private AI labs (Cohere, Mistral, OpenAI, Replicate — no registry footprint, UNVERIFIABLE individually) and public megacaps (Meta, IBM, Microsoft) that do NOT name CoreWeave in their filings. Per Heuristic 5, a hyperscaler/enterprise naming a cloud SUPPLIER is rare even for real relationships, so 0 megacap-side mentions for Meta/IBM/Microsoft is benign-explainable and not a contradiction. NVIDIA does corroborate (3 mentions). Net: customer list is partly corroborated (NVIDIA ecosystem, broad 123-filer EDGAR presence) but the specific enterprise names are not independently confirmed at the IPO date. Scored MODERATE — disclosed-but-not-counterparty-confirmed, with benign explanations, not SEVERE.

scores.claim_text: Self-disclosed material weaknesses in ICFR, $1.5B accumulated deficit, $8.0B total debt at 11-15% effective rates as of Dec 31 2024.
scores.M_check: going_concern_detector on CoreWeave CIK 0001769628 (constrained to prospectus-date disclosure; post-cutoff filings firewalled)
scores.M_value: At the IPO date the prospectus itself is the authority: management states existing cash + facility availability 'will be sufficient to meet obligations due within one year'; Deloitte & Touche (FY23/FY24) and RSM US (FY22) issued unqualified opinions with NO going-concern paragraph. (The detector defaulted to a post-cutoff 2026 10-K, which was disregarded under blinding discipline.)
scores.interpretation: This is a HONESTY-SIGNAL claim, not a marketing claim: CoreWeave affirmatively discloses material weaknesses in internal controls, a $1.5B accumulated deficit, $8.0B of debt at 10-15% rates, 62% single-customer concentration, and a stockholders' deficit. Per the honesty-alpha framework, candid disclosure of bad news is the framework's PASS pattern — the company is not masking its risks. Clean (non-going-concern) auditor opinions from Deloitte and RSM at the prospectus date corroborate that no substantial-doubt condition was identified as of the offering. Scored PASS: the negative facts are real and fully, honestly disclosed (and the underwriter syndicate of 18 banks incl. Morgan Stanley/JPM/Goldman reflects passing institutional diligence).
